issues.description: URL construction complects parsing, transformation, and remote-tagging assumptions in one function
issues.detail: use_koji_url_only treats a URL string as both the source of truth for NEVRA/arch and the template for a new URL, while silently encoding an external time-bound fact (that coreos-koji-tagger will later tag the build into coreos-pool). The value being produced is not actually 'the URL of an RPM that exists' — it's 'the URL of an RPM that we predict will exist after a separate async tag operation succeeds.' That's two different identities under one name. Decompose: parse URL -> NEVRA+arch value, then a separate pure function NEVRA+arch -> predicted coreos-pool URL, with the prediction's time semantics named in the function/variable.

issues.description: NEVRA is not a value here, it's the trailing path segment treated as a string
issues.detail: nevra = url.split('/')[-1] gives you a filename like 'foo-1.2-3.fc40.x86_64.rpm', not a NEVRA value. The code then indexes nevra[0] to get the Packages subdirectory letter. That works for ASCII-named packages but complects 'filename' with 'NEVRA' with 'first-letter bucket' — three different concepts wearing the same name. A small parse_rpm_filename function returning a record/dict {name, version, release, arch, filename} would make the value explicit, make the [0] bucket lookup honest (it's the first char of the package name, not 'nevra'), and let extract_arch_from_url be deleted entirely.

issues.description: extract_arch_from_url returns None silently; caller doesn't handle it
issues.detail: If the regex doesn't match, the function returns None, and the caller then does f'/latest/{arch}/Packages' which interpolates the string 'None' into the URL. No error, no log, no fail — just a wrong URL produced and written into rpms.lock.yaml. The time when this matters is exactly the time you don't want a silent failure: when the upstream URL format changes. Either raise on miss, or assert arch is in the known set at the call site. Make the failure mode loud.

issues.description: Word-boundary regex over the whole URL can match the wrong arch token
issues.detail: The regex searches the entire URL for any of the four arch strings with \b boundaries. URLs from Fedora's mirror layout generally include the arch as a path segment, but nothing in the contract guarantees the *first* match is the package arch — a mirror path, a koji tag name, or a future hostname containing 'x86_64' would silently win. The arch lives in a known position (either the path segment before 'Packages' in koji URLs, or parseable from the RPM filename suffix). Read it from the structured position you actually trust, don't scan the whole string and hope.

issues.description: koji_url_base and arch list are place-oriented config buried in code
issues.detail: The koji base URL, the path template '/latest/{arch}/Packages', and the supported arch list are all literals in functions. They are facts about the world (what koji's layout is, what arches CoreOS ships) that will change on a different cadence than this script. Promote them to module-level constants or a small config dict. Not blocking, but it would make the 'when does this fact change?' question answerable by reading one place.

issues.description: Dead code path: the coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location is now redundant
issues.detail: query_packages_location still prefers coreos-pool URLs when multiple repos return the same NEVRA, but generate_main now rewrites every non-coreos-pool URL into a coreos-pool URL anyway. The prioritization is no longer load-bearing — it's a vestige that will confuse the next reader about which layer owns the 'use coreos-pool' policy. Pick one place to own the rule. If the rewrite is the policy, the prioritization can be deleted; if the prioritization is a fast path, comment why both exist.

issues.description: Race-condition and untestable-locally caveats live in the PR description, not in the code
issues.detail: The PR description names two real properties of this design: a race between koji tagging and Konflux builds, and the inability to test rpms.lock.yaml changes locally. Those are facts about the time semantics of the produced value. A docstring on use_koji_url_only that names them — 'this URL is predicted, valid only after coreos-koji-tagger tags the build' — would put the warning where the next maintainer will read it.

review.summary: The patch trades a real DNF5 bug for a smaller, more honest pipeline, and that direction is right. But the new code complects three concerns under one name: parsing a URL into a NEVRA+arch value, constructing a predicted koji URL, and silently asserting a future tag operation will make that URL valid. The arch extraction is a whole-string regex with silent None on miss, and 'nevra' is actually a filename that gets indexed for a first-letter bucket. Decompose into (1) parse_rpm_filename -> structured value, (2) build_coreos_pool_url(parsed, arch) -> predicted URL, with the time-semantics of 'predicted' named in a docstring. Also reconcile the now-redundant coreos-pool prioritization in query_packages_location with the rewrite in generate_main — one of them should own the policy.
